newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent spikes up to a high of $23.50 on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent spikes up to a high of $23.50 on Iraq.

text.p: SIMEX Brent futures for October opened trading at $22.90 and touched a high of $23.50 on Tuesday after the United States it had launched cruise missiles at air defense targets in Iraq, brokers said.
"Its going through the roof," one broker told Reuters. The latest traded level of over $23.00 was way above its previous high of $22.68 recorded in mid-April.

The Pentagon said the attack was in retaliation for Iraqi military incursions against the Kurds in northern Iraq. Anti aircraft fire was also launched from positions in Bahgdad on Tuesday but was not immediately clear what it was aimed at.
When the United Nations decided on Sunday to delay the oil-for-food plan with Iraq, the prompt-month October contract jumped 82 cents to $21.80 and hit $22.00 on London's IPE.
After a lull for most of the morning, trading in the afternoon continued to be active as was seen on Monday when it recorded 1,402 lots, the highest since March 14.
The October contract recorded 300 lots on Tuesday.
The November Brent contract last traded at $22.60, up $1.47 a barrel from IPE close with 120 lots traded, while December last traded at $22.00, up $1.36, with 7 lots recorded.
